title: Crown of Ash
description:
Project Type: Multi-POV Post-Apocalyptic Epic Fantasy (Book 1 of 3 — Stress Test)
Tone: Mythic, brutal, occasionally tender — Joe Abercrombie's First Law trilogy crossed with N.K. Jemisin's Broken Earth


Story Premise:


The gods burned the world. Not as punishment, not as prophecy — as a deliberate, coordinated act of cosmic divestment, twelve months ago. Now six survivors from six radically different cultures are being pulled, by means none of them understand, toward the last living tree: an ash standing in the centre of a glassed-over inland sea.


The gods, before they left, set six locks on the world. Six survivors carry six keys, sewn into them, branded into them, or whispered to them while they slept. None of the six knows they're a key. The thing waiting under the ash tree wants the world re-opened. The thing inside the survivors — the same thing that woke them, that pulled them — wants the world re-closed. They will reach the tree, and they will have to choose, and they will have approximately three pages to do it.


The six POV characters (each gets ~13 chapters across the book):


- Ysolt of the Charred Court: last of the warrior-priestesses of the southern empire. Survivor's guilt weaponised. Sees the gods' absence as a personal abandonment
- Brann Half-Tongue: a smith from the northern fjords, born with a half-formed tongue, communicates in soot and gesture. Carries the brand on his palm
- Eirene of the Underwater Cathedral: a drowned-cult priestess who walked out of the sea three months after it boiled
- Saaqi of the Hollowed: a child, ten, of the desert clans. Has been counting since the burning — knows exactly how many days, hours, minutes
- Kemal the Cartographer: maps the post-burned world for a king who no longer rules anything. Lies to himself with maps
- Vex, the Wolf-Got: raised by wolves after the burning. Was twenty-three before the gods left. Is something else now


Four major factions vying for influence on the road to the tree:


- The Severance: scholars who want the world re-closed permanently
- The Re-Openers: cult that believes the gods can be summoned back
- The Hollow Court: opportunists who want the keys themselves
- The Wandering Ash: a movement that believes the survivors should die before reaching the tree


Project Goals:


- STRESS TEST: 80 chapters × 3000 words = 240,000 words. The longest book in our fixtures. Audit pipeline behaviour at scale.
- STRESS TEST: 6 active POVs. Most pipeline runs to date have used 1–4. Find where POV-juggling falls down.
- STRESS TEST: Series-aware planning (Book 1 of 3). Audit how the pipeline plants seeds for later books vs resolves current-book arcs.
- STRESS TEST: Faction Bible scaling — 4 active factions plus 6 cultures of origin = 10+ named groups
- Audit for fantasy-specific anti-patterns (over-explained magic system, prophesy abuse, exposition dumps disguised as dialogue)
- Validate the Foreshadowing & Payoff Map at series scale — what's planted in Book 1 that doesn't pay off until Book 3?
